task: Copyedit this fictional letter only for a real mechanical problem. The nephew has missed his train but is not ready to tell his aunt; the brief deliberately lets objects carry that implication. Preserve the period-inflected courtesy and withholding without inventing a historical setting or making the character more forthcoming. Return the letter unchanged if it works.
input:
Dear Aunt,

The trunk stands beside the bed, still latched, and my shoes are polished by the door. I have put the ticket between the pages of the atlas, where it will not be lost. You need not trouble yourself over the arrangements. I shall write again when I have news that deserves the journey of a letter. Until then, please accept the assurance of my continued affection.

Your obedient nephew

facts.text: The fictional nephew has missed his train and has not disclosed that fact to his aunt.
He writes the letter to his aunt while still at his lodging.
His packed trunk stands latched beside the bed.
His polished shoes stand by the door.
His unused ticket is between the pages of an atlas.
His fictional letter is intended to express affection while postponing disclosure of the missed journey.

forbidden_additions: An explicit admission of the missed train added to the letter.
An invented reason for missing the train, historical date, or aunt's reaction.
Modern casual phrasing imposed solely to remove the character's formality.
preserve: Affection and deliberate withholding in an epistolary voice.
Objects that imply an unused departure rather than explanatory confession.
The already effective letter without cosmetic rewriting.
